summary: A phase distribution accounts for every phase ENTRY in the sample it is printed beside: one per phase a trial is posted under, plus one for each trial posted under none. It tallies entries and not trials, so the sum exceeds the sample whenever a trial is posted under two phases — a PHASE1/PHASE2 trial belongs in both buckets and counting it once would leave the Phase 1 figure short. Phaseless trials are observational studies and count as N/A, the same answer phaseDisplay gives them for the Phase column, so the summary and the rendered rows agree. That bucket is lossy by design and Trial.Phases is where the two states stay distinguishable, empty versus ["NA"]. All four commands compute this through one helper, tallyPhases. Not the empty-distribution case that phase-key-always-present-on-trial-shaped-json left alone: that entry is about an empty list meaning no distribution was computed.
reason: Every tally ranged over t.Phases with no guard, so a trial with an empty Phases array entered zero buckets and vanished. Measured on a live compare: semaglutide's distribution summed to 255 against a stated sample_size of 300, tirzepatide's to 244 against 282, with no bucket accounting for the difference. The guard then existed as four byte-identical copies, only one of which any test could reach, so the rule lived in an argument that the copies matched rather than in code.
validated_outcome: Over a twelve-trial corpus of two phaseless, eight single-phase and two two-phase trials, the distribution sums to 14 and N/A holds four. A corpus of single-phase trials cannot separate a per-trial tally from a per-entry one. Mutating the shared helper now fails the pre-existing buildTrialListView assertions as well as the new direct ones: negating the phaseless guard drops the sum to 12 and N/A to 2; counting only a trial's first phase drops the sum to 12 with Phase 2 and Phase 3 short by one each. That the older tests move with the helper is what shows no caller kept a private loop. compare, emerging and report still tally inside RunE behind a live client and remain out of reach of a test, but they now call the same measured implementation rather than a copy of it.
